skill.name: env-config
skill.description: Guides Python and FastAPI projects through typed environment configuration, .env templates, dotenv loading, validation, and secret handling patterns.
skill.summary: Set up typed FastAPI environment settings with Pydantic, dotenv, and secret handling guidance.
skill.author: Awais68

security_audit.summary: Most external command and network detections are false positives from markdown code fences, inline examples, and localhost CORS values. Real risk remains because the skill intentionally guides work with .env files, secret names, environment variants, and a file-writing rotation example. No prompt injection, credential exfiltration intent, or unauthorized network behavior was found.

remediation.suggestion: Warn users before reading or editing .env files, prefer .env.example for shared context, and redact values from responses.
Restrict file paths, escape the key pattern, create backups, set safe permissions, and avoid printing secret-bearing paths or values.
Keep production examples as placeholders and direct users to managed secrets rather than local production .env files.

content.value_statement: Environment settings often spread across files and deployment targets. This skill provides typed FastAPI patterns for .env templates, validation, and secret handling.
actual_capabilities: Defines Pydantic BaseSettings patterns for FastAPI projects.
Shows .env.example, local .env, staging, and production file layouts.
Documents dotenv loading and cached settings access.
Covers database URLs, JWT settings, Redis, logging, and CORS values.
Includes startup validation and an illustrative secret rotation script.
limitations: Focused on Python and FastAPI projects; other stacks need adaptation.
Does not connect to a real cloud secrets manager API.
Placeholder secrets must be replaced before any deployed use.
The rotation script needs backups and path validation before use.

use_cases.title: Bootstrap FastAPI Configuration
use_cases.description: Create typed settings, required fields, and dotenv loading for a new FastAPI service.

use_cases.title: Separate Deployment Environments
use_cases.description: Plan local, staging, and production configuration files with clear ownership boundaries.

use_cases.title: Review Secret Handling
use_cases.description: Check that sensitive values use safer types, generated secrets, and non-committed local files.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Starter Config
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new FastAPI project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a basic FastAPI environment configuration plan with required app, database, JWT, logging, and CORS settings.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Settings Class
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Pydantic settings class for my FastAPI service. Include required fields, defaults, validation notes, and secret handling.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Multi-Environment Files
prompt_templates.scenario: Separate development, staging, and production settings.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan environment files for development, staging, and production. Explain which files may be committed and which must stay private.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Existing Configuration
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of an existing app.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my environment configuration design for security, deployment safety, validation gaps, and secret rotation risks.

output_examples.input: Set up configuration for a new FastAPI project.
output: A settings plan with application, database, JWT, Redis, logging, and CORS sections.
A list of required and optional variables with validation notes.
Guidance on which values belong in local files versus deployment settings.

output_examples.input: Review whether our .env files are safe to commit.
output: A commit policy that allows templates and blocks local or production secret files.
A checklist for placeholder values, generated secrets, and ignored private files.
Warnings about copying weak sample secrets into deployed environments.
A safer rotation workflow with backups, path limits, and validation before writing changes.
Advice to prefer managed secrets in production.
A reminder to redact secret values from logs and review output.

best_practices: Use committed templates for variable names and keep real .env files private.
Generate unique secrets for each environment and rotate them through controlled workflows.
Validate configuration at startup and redact secret values from logs and shared output.
anti_patterns: Copying sample secrets into staging or production deployments.
Committing local, staging, or production .env files with real credentials.
Using a file-writing rotation script without backups, path checks, or permission controls.

faq.question: Does this skill execute deployment commands?
faq.answer: No. It provides configuration guidance and examples for Python and FastAPI projects.

faq.question: Can it manage production secrets directly?
faq.answer: No. It recommends production secret management patterns but does not call a secrets manager API.

faq.question: Should I share real .env values with the assistant?
faq.answer: No. Share variable names, templates, or redacted values unless you explicitly approve secret handling.

faq.question: Is the .env.example file safe to commit?
faq.answer: Yes, if it contains only variable names and placeholders, not real credentials.

faq.question: What projects fit this skill best?
faq.answer: It fits Python and FastAPI services that use Pydantic settings and dotenv-style local configuration.

faq.question: What should I review before using the rotation example?
faq.answer: Add backups, restrict file paths, validate keys, and avoid exposing secret values in logs or output.
